title: Server-side JSX with jsx-async-runtime
description: Everything jsx-async-runtime renders on the server: promises, iterables and other values as children, render props, request context via 'this', overriding how JSX turns into HTML, head management, i18n, Declarative Shadow DOM and unit tests for components.

title: Streaming with jsx-async-runtime
description: Async components don't block the page: jsx-async-runtime streams HTML as soon as it is ready, in order, in parallel or out of order, from async iterables or a ReadableStream.

title: Client-side apps with jsx-async-runtime
description: Render the same JSX components on the server and in the browser with jsx-async-runtime, without React, a virtual DOM or hydration: from simple widgets to apps that work with and without JavaScript, and streamed async trees.

title: Client-side games with jsx-async-runtime
description: Games where jsx-async-runtime renders every frame in the browser: animation, input and game logic with plain JSX components.

title: Server-rendered websites and apps
description: Render pages on the server with content from a remote API, JSON data or Markdown with MDX, and build interactive apps with plain HTML forms. No client-side JavaScript needed: view transitions make page changes feel smooth.

title: Images, JSON and other content types
description: Routes aren't limited to HTML: they can return images, SVG, JSON, XML, a live stream of Server-Sent Events or any other content type.

title: Security, errors and post-processing
description: Protect routes with basic auth or sessions, sign cookies, block injected scripts and stop bots with a proof-of-work captcha. Catch errors and transform the final HTML before it is sent to the browser.

title: Hypermedia with HTMX
description: Every Jeasx route can return an HTML fragment, so hypermedia libraries like HTMX and Fixi can update parts of a page with markup rendered on the server.

title: JavaScript libraries and frameworks
description: Add islands of interactivity to server-rendered pages with the JavaScript library or framework you already know.
